text: About 2,700 years ago, the Scythians ruled the grasslands north of the Black Sea.
They were horse riders who moved with their herds of horses, cattle and sheep.
src: Iranian-speaking horse nomads who dominated the steppe north of the Black Sea from the 7th to the 3rd century BCE / in present-day Ukraine, southern Russia and Crimea
horse nomads / Herds of horses, cattle and sheep moved between summer and winter pastures along the great rivers

text: Women and children lived in felt-covered wagons, while the men rode as archers on horseback.
Their eastern relatives, the Saka, buried this “Golden Man” in thousands of gold ornaments.
src: the women and children lived in wagons covered with felt and drawn by oxen while the men rode / all of them mounted archers
the Issyk kurgan near Almaty held a Saka warrior, the “Golden Man”, clothed in thousands of gold ornaments / their eastern kin, the Saka

text: Kings were buried under great earth mounds, with horses, treasure and servants killed at the funeral.
src: The royal kurgans of the lower Dnieper, such as Chertomlyk and Solokha, have confirmed the core of this account: kings lie there with attendants, horses and treasure / a concubine, a cupbearer, a cook, a groom, a servant and a messenger, all strangled

text: Scythian art is full of golden animals: stags, panthers, birds of prey and griffins.
Greek craftsmen also made treasures for them, like this vase showing Scythian warriors.
src: Their gold work of stags, panthers and griffins / Stags with their legs folded beneath them, panthers curled into a ring, birds of prey, boars and griffins
Greek goldsmiths ... made works for Scythian patrons that show the Scythians themselves / an electrum vase from Kul-Oba shows warriors stringing a bow

text: They sold grain, hides, fish and slaves to Greek cities, for wine, olive oil and pottery.
When the Persian king Darius invaded, they refused to fight and drew back until he left.
src: The Greek cities bought grain, hides, fish and slaves from the interior and sold wine, olive oil, painted pottery and fine metalwork
Led by Idanthyrsus, they refused battle and retreated eastward ... and Darius withdrew across the Danube

text: Other nomads later took the grasslands, but Scythian kings like Skilurus held on in Crimea.
Their gold now fills museums in Kyiv and Saint Petersburg.
src: From the 3rd century BCE the Sarmatians ... took over much of the steppe / The Scythians held on in Crimea ... a Late Scythian kingdom / its king Skilurus struck coins at Olbia / survived, much reduced, until Neapolis was destroyed in the second half of the 3rd century CE
their gold fills the Hermitage and the Museum of Historical Treasures of Ukraine in Kyiv / now in the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg
